answer: The protocol requires 9,000 megabytes of memory-hard work to gate each agent, where the verifier maps memory to a secure ledge to prevent task cloning. Each node maintains a unique heap, functioning like a pulse of compute that triggers a penalty if overlapping buffers emerge. If an honest agent pays for one unit of cost, 1,000 fakes incur 1,000 times that cost, as each must populate distinct memory arrays. The network confirms these sessions against a sonnet of state snapshots; any reused data leads to instant slashing and a lockout for the duration of the current validation window.
